fullPassage:
[1번] The Faroe Islands are a group of islands in the North Atlantic. Although they are controlled by Denmark, they have their own government. The people of the islands traditionally hunt pilot whales. They have done this for centuries, so whale meat and blubber are important parts of the local diet. The government insists the killing of whales is not done for profit. Most of the whale meat and blubber is distributed for free to the local community, although some is sold in supermarkets. Multiple hunts are held each year under the strict supervision of the local government. There is a law that says each killing must take place as quickly and efficiently as possible. The government claims that the average annual catch is only about 800 whales and that this is a small percentage of the overall pilot whale population. However, environmental groups still question whether this practice should be allowed to continue.

[2번] Broken heart syndrome, also known as takotsubo syndrome (TTS), is a condition that occurs when stress weakens the heart's ability to pump blood. TTS can occur after stressful events such as the loss of a family member or a natural disaster. Surprisingly, researchers say people can also get TTS when happy things occur, sometimes referring to this as "happy heart syndrome." A researcher discovered this while analyzing data from 1,750 patients with takotsubo syndrome. Of the 485 patients diagnosed after emotional events, 20 had experienced happy events. The researcher concluded that the brain reacts similarly to extremely positive and negative events, so both can result in takotsubo syndrome.

[3번] Imagine you take your bicycle to a repair shop. You expect the workers at the shop to do what you paid them to do, which is to fix your bicycle. If they do a good job, you will be back again next time for bike repairs. If they do a bad job, however, you will look for a new repair shop. The same is true with governments. It is our job as citizens to make sure that government does what is expected. If they do a good job, we can trust them in the future. If they don't, we can explain why we won't vote for them again. This kind of participation in government is important. How much effort we put into participating depends on how well we think the government is doing. If we are satisfied, we will do very little besides voting. But if we are dissatisfied, we will probably take other types of action.

[4번] Dr. Viktor Emil Frankl was an Austrian psychiatrist who thought that feeling emotional pain was a natural part of life, and that humans have the ability to choose how to respond to situations. But most importantly, he believed that people's main motivation in life is the search for meaning. According to Frankl, in order to find this meaning in their lives, people have to change their attitude toward unavoidable suffering. For example, Frankl was helping a man who was severely depressed after his wife's death. He asked the man to think about what would have happened if he had died first and his wife had been forced to live without him. The man realized his own grief and pain meant that his wife did not have to experience what he was going through. This helped end his depression.

[5번] Many products for sale at local supermarkets contain a chemical called bisphenol A, more commonly known as BPA. BPA can be found in plastics used to make food containers and baby bottles. It is also used to protect the inside of metal food cans. These products can cause people to be exposed to BPA through their diet. This is because BPA may leak out of these containers and into the food itself. BPA is harmful to the body because its structure is similar to that of natural hormones. This similarity makes it easy for vital bodily functions to be negatively affected. Whether or not BPA should be banned is controversial, but many experts consider it unwise to use products that contain BPA.

[6번] When we experience feelings of fatigue, they may seem to be physical. Yet, studies show that these feelings don't actually come from the body. Even when people report being exhausted from exercise, there is still enough energy in their muscle tissues to continue on for several minutes more. This is because it is actually the brain that sends us the message to stop exercising before we reach our physical limit in order to prevent potential injuries. However, scientists have found it possible to fool the brain. For example, running a small electrical current through their brain increased cyclists' output by 10%. And other athletes have shown improvements in their performance in hot conditions when given incorrect information about the temperature.

[7번] In today's interconnected world, people rely heavily on a handful of dominant languages. This causes a serious problem, even though it improves international cooperation, by threatening vulnerable languages. Many languages slowly die out as the younger generations first become bilingual and then gradually abandon their traditional language. It is important that efforts are made to prevent this from happening. Language is woven together with culture, and it reflects what is important to those who speak it. As a culture develops, its language grows and changes with it. But when a language is lost, the culture is at risk. Without a language to pass down stories and lessons from the past, the culture could simply disappear.

[8번] The concept of karma suggests that every action has a consequence, whether in this life or the next. Essentially, karma is like a seed; what you plant, you will eventually harvest. For example, a man kept harassing others online under the cloak of anonymity. Eventually, however, his identity was exposed and legal action was taken against him. In a different instance, a CEO of a large company paid the necessary, expensive fees to dispose of waste from its factory correctly, while her rivals simply dumped their waste from their factories into local rivers. A government investigation later revealed the behavior of her competitors. They were forced to pay massive fines and eventually went bankrupt. These examples remind us that living a moral life matters, even if we don't immediately see the results of our actions.

questions.passage: The Faroe Islands are a group of islands in the North Atlantic. Although they are controlled by Denmark, they have their own government. The people of the islands traditionally hunt pilot whales. They have done this for centuries, so whale meat and blubber are important parts of the local diet. The government insists the killing of whales is not done for profit. Most of the whale meat and blubber is (A)[collected / distributed] for free to the local community, although some is sold in supermarkets. Multiple hunts are held each year under the strict supervision of the local government. There is a law that says each killing must take place as quickly and efficiently as possible. The government claims that the average (B)[annual / occasional] catch is only about 800 whales and that this is a small percentage of the overall pilot whale population. However, environmental groups still question whether this practice should be allowed to (C)[stop / continue].
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) distributed=분배되는 / collected=수거되는 (B) annual=연간의 / occasional=가끔의 (C) continue=계속되다 / stop=멈추다
det.analysis:
① collected: 무료로 '수거'? 지역사회에 '분배(distributed)'됨
② distributed—annual—continue: 고기는 무료로 '분배'되고, '연간' 어획량을 언급하며, 환경단체는 이 관행이 '계속'되어야 하는지 의문을 제기 ←정답
③ occasional/stop: 가끔의/멈추다는 문맥과 반대
④ collected/occasional/stop: 모두 문맥과 반대
det.tip: 고기는 distributed(분배), average annual(연간) catch, allowed to continue(계속) 흐름

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) diagnosed=진단받은 / cured=치료된 (B) emotional=감정적인 / physical=신체적인 (C) extremely=극도로 / slightly=약간
det.analysis:
① cured: 감정적 사건 뒤 '치료된' 환자? 진단(diagnosed)의 맥락과 반대
② physical/slightly: '신체적' 사건이 아닌 감정적 사건이며, '약간' 긍정·부정은 약함
③ cured/physical/slightly: 모두 문맥과 반대
④ diagnosed — emotional — extremely: '감정적' 사건 후 '진단받은' 환자, 뇌는 '극도로' 긍정·부정 사건에 반응 ←정답
det.tip: emotional(감정적) 사건 뒤 diagnosed(진단), extremely(극도로) positive/negative

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 trust와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) depressed=우울한 / delighted=기뻐하는 (B) grief=슬픔 / joy=기쁨 (C) experience=겪다 / avoid=피하다

det.tip: 우울한(depressed) 남자, 그의 슬픔(grief), 아내가 고통을 겪지(experience) 않아도 됨의 흐름

questions.passage:
(A) A dishonest employee tried to <u>leak</u> the company's secret plans to reporters before the official announcement was made.

(B) BPA may <u>leak</u> out of plastic containers and mix into the food we eat every day.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)에서 밑줄 친 leak의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: leak: (A) (비밀을) 누설하다 (B) (액체가) 새어 나오다
det.analysis:
① (A) (비밀을) 누설하다 (B) (액체가) 새어 나오다: 직원이 기밀을 누설하고, BPA가 용기에서 새어 나온다 ←정답
② (A) 새어 나오다 (B) 누설하다: (A)(B) 의미가 뒤바뀜
③ (A) 누설하다 (B) 누설하다: (B)는 액체 누출이므로 부적절
④ (A) 넘쳐흐르다 (B) 새어 나오다: (A)의 의미가 부정확
det.tip: leak의 다의어: (비밀·정보를) 누설하다 vs (액체가) 새다

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) insists=주장하다 / denies=부인하다 (B) strict=엄격한 / loose=느슨한 (C) quickly=빠르게 / slowly=느리게
det.analysis:

③ denies/loose/slowly: 모두 문맥과 반대
④ insists—strict—quickly: 이익 목적이 아니라고 '주장'하고, '엄격한' 감독하에, '빠르게' 처리되어야 한다 ←정답

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) concluded=결론지었다 / doubted=의심했다 (B) similarly=비슷하게 / differently=다르게 (C) result in=~을 초래하다 / prevent=막다
det.analysis:
① doubted: 연구자가 '의심했다'? 데이터로 밝혔으므로 concluded(결론지었다)가 맞음
② concluded — similarly — result in: 뇌가 긍정·부정 사건에 '비슷하게' 반응해 둘 다 병을 '초래한다'고 '결론지었다' ←정답
③ differently/prevent: '다르게' 반응하는데 둘 다 초래한다는 모순, prevent(막다)도 반대
④ doubted/differently: 둘 다 문맥과 반대
det.tip: 연구자가 concluded(결론), 뇌가 similarly(비슷하게) 반응, 둘 다 result in(초래)

How much effort we put into participating depends on how well we think the government is doing. If we are (C)[dissatisfied / satisfied], we will do very little besides voting. questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) good=좋은 / bad=나쁜 (B) trust=신뢰하다 / doubt=의심하다 (C) satisfied=만족한 / dissatisfied=불만족한
det.analysis:
① good — trust — satisfied: 일을 잘하면(good) 미래에 신뢰할 수 있고(trust), 만족하면(satisfied) 거의 아무것도 안 한다 ←정답
② bad: 일을 나쁘게 하면 신뢰? (A) 문맥과 반대
③ doubt/dissatisfied: 잘하는데 의심? 만족하는데 불만족? 문맥과 반대
④ bad/doubt: (A)(B) 모두 문맥과 반대
det.tip: 잘하면(good) 신뢰하고(trust), 만족하면(satisfied) 별 행동 안 한다는 긍정 흐름

questions.passage: Dr. Viktor Emil Frankl was an Austrian psychiatrist who thought that feeling ①<u>emotional</u> pain was a natural part of life, and that humans have the ability to choose how to respond to situations. But most importantly, he believed that people's main motivation in life is the search for ②<u>meaning</u>. According to Frankl, in order to find this meaning in their lives, people have to change their ③<u>attitude</u> toward unavoidable ④<u>comfort</u>. For example, Frankl was helping a man who was severely depressed after his wife's death. He asked the man to think about what would have happened if he had died first and his wife had been forced to live without him. The man realized his own grief and pain meant that his wife did not have to experience what he was going through. This helped end his depression.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① emotional=감정적인 ② meaning=의미 ③ attitude=태도 ④ suffering→comfort(부적절): 피할 수 없는 것은 '고통'이지 '안락함'이 아님
det.analysis:
① emotional: 감정적 고통 — 적절
② meaning: 의미의 추구 — 적절
③ attitude: 태도를 바꾸다 — 적절
④ comfort: 피할 수 없는 '안락함'? 원문은 unavoidable suffering(피할 수 없는 고통) ←정답
det.tip: unavoidable(피할 수 없는)과 어울리는 것은 suffering(고통). comfort(안락함)는 반대

questions.passage: Many products for sale at local supermarkets ①<u>contain</u> a chemical called bisphenol A, more commonly known as BPA. BPA can be found in plastics used to make food containers and baby bottles. It is also used to ②<u>protect</u> the inside of metal food cans. These products can cause people to be exposed to BPA through their diet. This is because BPA may leak out of these containers and into the food itself. BPA is ③<u>helpful</u> to the body because its structure is similar to that of natural hormones. This similarity makes it easy for vital bodily functions to be negatively affected. Whether or not BPA should be ④<u>banned</u> is controversial, but many experts consider it unwise to use products that contain BPA.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① contain=함유하다 ② protect=보호하다 ③ harmful→helpful (부적절) ④ banned=금지된
det.analysis:
① contain: 제품이 화학물질을 함유한다 — 적절
② protect: 금속캔 내부를 보호하는 데 쓰인다 — 적절
③ helpful: BPA가 몸에 '이롭다'? 뒤에 해로운 이유가 이어지므로 harmful이 원문 ←정답
④ banned: 금지되어야 하는지 논쟁적 — 적절
det.tip: BPA는 몸에 harmful(해로운). helpful은 정반대

questions.passage: Multiple hunts are __________ (hold) each year under the strict supervision of the local government.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: hold(동사: 개최하다) → held(과거분사). be동사 + p.p. 수동태 'are held(열린다/개최된다)'
det.analysis: hold를 과거분사 held로 변환. 'Multiple hunts are held' = '여러 차례의 사냥이 열린다' — 사냥이 '열리는' 것이므로 be + p.p. 수동태 필요
det.tip: hunts are _____ → 사냥이 열리는 것(수동) → be + p.p. → held

questions.passage: A researcher discovered this while __________ (analyze) data from 1,750 patients with takotsubo syndrome.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: analyze(동사: 분석하다) → analyzing(분사: 분석하면서). while + V-ing 분사구문
det.analysis: analyze를 -ing 형태 analyzing으로 변환. 'while analyzing data' = '데이터를 분석하는 동안/분석하면서' — 접속사 while 뒤에서 동시동작을 나타내는 분사(V-ing)가 필요해요.
det.tip: while _____ = ~하면서 → 분사(V-ing) → analyzing

questions.passage: If we are __________ (satisfy), we will do very little besides voting.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: satisfy(만족시키다) → satisfied(만족한). be동사 뒤 형용사/과거분사 형태
det.analysis: satisfy를 satisfied로 변환. 'If we are satisfied'(우리가 만족하면) — be동사(are) 뒤에는 형용사 역할을 하는 과거분사 satisfied가 필요
det.tip: we are _____ → be동사 뒤 감정 형용사 → satisfied

questions.passage: Frankl thought that __________ (feel) emotional pain was a natural part of life.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: feel(동사: 느끼다) → feeling(동명사: 느끼는 것). 주어 자리의 동명사
det.analysis: feel을 동명사 feeling으로 변환. '감정적 고통을 느끼는 것(Feeling)은' 삶의 자연스러운 부분이다 — 주어 자리에 동명사(-ing)가 필요
det.tip: 주어 자리 '~하는 것' → 동명사(-ing). feeling emotional pain was ~

questions.passage: Many products for sale at local supermarkets contain a chemical called bisphenol A, more __________ (common) known as BPA. BPA can be found in plastics used to make food containers and baby bottles.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: common(형용사: 흔한) → commonly(부사: 흔히). 과거분사 known을 수식하는 부사
det.analysis: common(형용사: 흔한)을 부사 commonly로 변환. 'more commonly known as BPA' = '더 흔히 BPA로 알려진' — 과거분사 known을 수식하므로 부사 형태가 필요
det.tip: known(분사)을 수식 → 부사 -ly → commonly
